question: Did the Pass-1 layout-stratified SAMPLER (99b853cc) or rule 4's 'code is REQUIRED, never null' prompt clarification (b35b9666) fix NV's two domain codes and its description truncation between 288c64f1 and 7da92182?
answer: THE SAMPLER. Confirmed by controlled A/B.
method: Three arms on ONE frozen extraction (outputs/08-26-26-2/NV-extraction.json), all at 14374dba, all --no-cache, all graded by evaluation.eval_detector.evaluate_state. The ONLY thing that varies between arm A and arm B is which blocks Pass-1 sees: arm B monkeypatches detector._sample_blocks_for_depth_map back to the pre-99b853cc stride implementation. Rule 4's prompt clarification is present in BOTH arms, which is what exonerates it.

C_depth_map_disabled._source: paper/results/task3_20260826 off-arm; included because it brackets the effect

conclusion: Reverting ONLY the sampler reproduces BOTH previously-unattributed failures: the same two domain mismatches (NV-DOM-02 S->Science, NV-DOM-03 T->TECH) that 288c64f1 recorded, and the description truncation (2/3). Nothing else changed, so the sampler is the cause of both.
Rule 4's prompt clarification (b35b9666) is EXONERATED: it is present in both arms and the failure returns anyway.

The effect is bracketed by arm C. Disabling the depth map entirely gives 44/46 with the same domain pair, so NV's domain-code failure is depth-map-mediated and the sampler determines whether the map is good enough to prevent it.

Arm B scores 43/46, slightly WORSE than the 44/46 that 288c64f1 recorded, because of a third mismatch (NV-SUB-06 T.TT -> TT) that is ordinary detector sampling variance. The two DOMAIN mismatches are the stable, reproducible part and are what the A/B turns on.
